relevance_to_rcdome: This framework could inform RCDome's approach to detecting and mitigating hallucinated content by modeling perception as prediction error minimization.

item: Prediction error minimization as a mechanism
verbatim_sentence: In standard PP, this is achieved by the reciprocal exchange of top-down perceptual predictions and bottom-up (sensory) prediction error signals in a continual process of prediction error minimisation, which approximates Bayesian inference on the causes of sensory signals.
relevance_to_rcdome: RCDome could apply similar iterative error-correction to validate AI-generated video content against source evidence.

item: Precision-weighted balance between predictions and errors
verbatim_sentence: Importantly, the outcome of this (approximate) inference process depends on the relative influence of (top-down) predictions and (bottom-up) prediction errors, a balance which is mediated by the estimated precision (informally, the ‘reliability’) of sensory signals relative to perceptual predictions ( Yuille and Kersten, 2006 ; Fletcher and Frith, 2009 ; Friston and Kiebel, 2009 ; Zarkali et al., 2019 ).
relevance_to_rcdome: This suggests RCDome should weight the reliability of evidence sources when generating scientific videos to reduce hallucination.

item: Aberrant inference as cause of hallucinations
verbatim_sentence: Within this framework, VHs can be broadly understood as resulting from aberrant inference in which this balance is disrupted in some way ( Friston, 2005 ; Powers et al., 2016 ; Corlett et al., 2019 ; Zarkali et al., 2019 ).
relevance_to_rcdome: This highlights that hallucinations arise from disrupted inference, which RCDome must avoid by anchoring generated content to verifiable evidence.

verbatim_sentence: Some researchers have interpreted Neurodegenerative VHs as resulting from overly strong perceptual predictions which overwhelm sensory prediction error signals ( Powers et al., 2016 ; O’Callaghan et al., 2017 ).
relevance_to_rcdome: This suggests that over-reliance on prior assumptions can cause hallucination, so RCDome should prioritize sensory/evidence signals over model priors.

verbatim_sentence: Others have focused on psychedelic VHs and adopted a hierarchical perspective, suggesting that psychedelic hallucinations occur due to a relaxation of high-level perceptual predictions (or Bayesian ‘priors’), which has the effect of increasing the influence of bottom-up signalling on perceptual inference ( Alonso et al., 2015 ; Swanson, 2018 ; Timmermann et al., 2018 ; Carhart-Harris and Friston, 2019 ).
relevance_to_rcdome: This indicates that weakening top-down priors can increase bottom-up evidence influence, which RCDome can emulate by grounding content in raw data.

verbatim_sentence: To shed light on this question, we take a computational neurophenomenology approach ( Suzuki et al., 2017 ; Ramstead et al., 2022 ).
relevance_to_rcdome: This approach models perceptual experience, which could inspire RCDome to benchmark generated videos against phenomenological accuracy.

verbatim_sentence: Neurophenomenology emphasises the importance of capturing first-person descriptions of phenomena of interest (such as VHs) that are amenable to neurocognitive methodologies ( Lutz, 2002 ; Lutz et al., 2002 ; Gould et al., 2014 ).
relevance_to_rcdome: This principle suggests RCDome should incorporate user or expert verification of generated content to ensure alignment with observed reality.

item: Categorization of visual hallucinations by complexity
verbatim_sentence: VHs can generally be categorised as being either simple (e.g., shapes, flashes or grid-like lattice patterns) or complex (e.g., well-defined recognisable forms, such as objects or people).
relevance_to_rcdome: This provides a taxonomy for classifying hallucination types, which can inform detection criteria for AI-generated visual content in RCDome videos.

item: Veridicality as a measure of hallucination realism
verbatim_sentence: Neurodegenerative and CBS complex VHs typically display a high degree of perceptual veridicality.
relevance_to_rcdome: Veridicality assessment can be used to evaluate whether AI-generated scientific visuals match real-world perceptual fidelity, aiding hallucination mitigation.

item: Simulating hallucination phenomenology via coupled neural networks
verbatim_sentence: To simulate these specific aspects of hallucinatory phenomenology, we used the coupled neural network architecture of Nguyen et al. (2016) , which combines pre-trained classifier (DCNN) and generative (DGN) networks, to generate synthetic snapshots of aetiologically distinct VHs (see Materials and methods).
relevance_to_rcdome: This method could inspire RCDome to use coupled networks to generate controlled hallucination examples for testing evidence-anchored video accuracy.

item: Using visual seeds to drive hallucinations
verbatim_sentence: In contrast, anecdotal reports of psychedelic complex VHs describe them as frequently being driven by visual ‘seeds’ from within a perceived scene, bearing similarity to the everyday phenomenon of ‘pareidolia’—or ‘seeing patterns in noise’ ( Kometer and Vollenweider, 2018 ; Preller and Vollenweider, 2018 ; Swanson, 2018 ).
relevance_to_rcdome: This highlights how hallucinations can be anchored to visual input, which RCDome could leverage to ensure generated video content remains tied to source evidence.

item: GenerativeAM constrains outputs to realistic images
verbatim_sentence: Using this approach Nguyen et al. (2016) found that GenerativeAM produced output images that were much more realistic than those produced by ClassicalAM.
relevance_to_rcdome: This shows a method to reduce unrealistic AI-generated content, which could help RCDome avoid visual hallucinations in scientific videos.

verbatim_sentence: Previous studies using ClassicalAM have shown that it typically produces unrealistic, uninterpretable images ( Erhan et al., 2009 ; Mahendran and Vedaldi, 2014 ; Simonyan et al., 2014 ).
relevance_to_rcdome: Highlights a known failure mode in AI visualization that RCDome must avoid to maintain evidence-anchored accuracy.

item: Simulating hallucination with and without natural image prior
verbatim_sentence: To simulate differences in the veridicality of aetiologically distinct VHs, we generated synthetic VHs both with (GenerativeAM; high veridicality), and without (ClassicalAM; low veridicality), the natural image prior provided by the DGN.
relevance_to_rcdome: This method of controlling veridicality via image priors could inform RCDome's approach to anchoring generated video content in real-world evidence.

item: Iteration number as a control for veridicality
verbatim_sentence: Therefore, generating synthetic VHs using increasing numbers of iterations provides an additional inbuilt method of manipulating veridicality, as the veridicality of synthetic VHs decreases with increasing iteration number.
relevance_to_rcdome: This suggests that controlling iteration count in generative processes could help RCDome maintain factual accuracy in scientific videos.

item: Error function selection for target neuron control
verbatim_sentence: A key challenge when designing network visualisation techniques centres on the parameters of the error function used to select target neuron(s).
relevance_to_rcdome: This highlights the importance of precise error function design to avoid unintended hallucinations in RCDome's generated content.

item: Deep-Dream error function for input-dependent activation
verbatim_sentence: In contrast, the Deep-Dream error function, used in our previous simulations of hallucinatory phenomenology ( Mordvintsev et al., 2015 ; Suzuki et al., 2017 ), returns errors for all the neurons within a selected layer of the DCNN that were activated by the visual features of the input image.
relevance_to_rcdome: This input-dependent activation method could help RCDome ensure generated video content stays anchored to source evidence rather than drifting into hallucination.

item: Simulating hallucination via error function selection
verbatim_sentence: To simulate spontaneous VHs we used an error function that is not dependent on the input image (Fixed), and to simulate VHs that are driven by visual ‘seeds’ from within a perceived scene we used an error function that is dependent on the input image (Deep-Dream) to represent the apparent dependency between visual input and hallucinatory content (i.e., the lower spontaneity) reported in psychedelic VHs.
relevance_to_rcdome: This method of controlling hallucination by altering error functions could inform how RCDome anchors generated video content to source evidence, reducing ungrounded outputs.

verbatim_sentence: Based on our previous research ( Suzuki et al., 2017 ), we reasoned that simple hallucinatory phenomenology could be simulated by restricting the layer that AM terminates to a lower layer of the DCNN, resulting in an overemphasis of low-level visual features extracted by these layers during training ( Figure 1 , bottom).
relevance_to_rcdome: This layer-based control could guide RCDome in selecting appropriate feature depths to prevent over-abstracted or fabricated visual details in scientific videos.

verbatim_sentence: To investigate if synthetic psychedelic VHs were phenomenologically similar to psychedelic experiences, we used a one-tailed, one-sample t test using the test variable of the sample mean and a chance level of 0.5 (50%) to compare the ratio of responses between psychedelic and Neurodegenerative synthetic VHs for both simple and complex blocks separately.
relevance_to_rcdome: This benchmark method could be adapted to evaluate whether RCDome's evidence-anchored videos are perceived as accurate versus hallucinated by comparing viewer responses against chance.

verbatim_sentence: A Bayes Factor (BF) greater than 3 was taken to indicate sensitive evidence for the hypothesis that participants selected simulations of psychedelic VHs at a higher-than-chance frequency, whilst a BF < 1/3 was taken to indicate sensitive evidence for the null hypothesis.
relevance_to_rcdome: This provides a statistical framework to assess whether RCDome's video content is reliably distinguished from hallucinated alternatives.

relevance_to_rcdome: RCDome's evidence-anchored scientific videos must align with such regulatory standards to ensure safety and ethics in clinical visual content.

item: Rigorous regulatory and validation processes for clinical algorithms
verbatim_sentence: The development of more advanced algorithms suited for clinical use should undergo a rigorous regulatory and validation processes like any other medical device or software.
relevance_to_rcdome: RCDome's video generation algorithms should be validated rigorously to maintain evidence-anchored accuracy in scientific content.

item: Improving accuracy and reliability of anatomic images
verbatim_sentence: To harness the full potential of text-to-image models in plastic surgery, future developments must focus on improving the accuracy and reliability of anatomic images.
relevance_to_rcdome: RCDome's videos must prioritize accuracy and reliability to prevent hallucinated anatomical details in scientific evidence.

verbatim_sentence: This involves expanding and diversifying training datasets with clinical plastic-surgery data.
relevance_to_rcdome: RCDome can mitigate hallucination by using diverse, clinically relevant datasets for training its video generation models.

item: Systematic evaluation in real-world clinical applications
verbatim_sentence: It is also essential for future studies to systematically evaluate the effectiveness of these models in real-world clinical applications.
relevance_to_rcdome: RCDome should adopt systematic real-world evaluation benchmarks to verify the evidence-anchored quality of its scientific videos.
